title: A slow call under the new shortened budget is treated as an outage and switches the provider off for every user for 60 seconds
impact: Today Claude's timeout for generate()/generateStructured() dropped from 12 s to 8 s, and Groq gets whatever is left (about 4 s). Any timeout at that reduced budget counts as 'unreachable', and Cache::put('ai:provider-cooldown:<name>') then skips that provider for every user and every feature for AI_PROVIDER_COOLDOWN_SECONDS. A healthy provider can easily answer slowly. EventController calls generateStructured(..., 2400) for the event plan, which allows Claude up to 3,600 output tokens and takes well over 8 s. So one officer generating an event plan times Claude out and switches it off for everyone for a minute. Groq then times out at about 4 s on the same plan and is switched off too. For that minute every AI feature (briefings, Ask AI, finance summaries) shows deterministic text to everyone. The test only covers a probe that reports itself down; it never checks whether the provider was actually slow or broken.
fix: Start a cooling-off only for a failure that says nothing about our own budget. (1) Connection failures before any response: Claude's APIConnectionException whose previous is a Guzzle ConnectException without cURL error 28, and Groq's ConnectionException whose message lacks 'cURL error 28'. (2) A timeout, but only when the call ran with its full configured timeout (timeBudget === null or >= the configured seconds). In both services, set $this->unreachable only in those cases (for example, record $this->budgeted = $this->timeBudget !== null && $this->timeBudget < $configured in requestSeconds() and require !$this->budgeted for a timeout). Add a test: a ClaudeProbe that times out under a 4 s budget must not start the cooling-off, and one that times out under its full timeout must.

title: Streaming conversation: the 60 s 'total' timeout is really an idle read timeout, connect_timeout is ignored, and a stalled stream never starts the cooling-off
impact: The SDK does stream: it wraps a Guzzle client in StreamingHttpClient with stream => true, so deltas arrive as they are generated, which is good. But StreamHandler turns 'timeout' into PHP's http-context read timeout, which is per read. I checked this with a local SSE server and the same Guzzle setup: with timeout 3 a stream that kept sending bytes ran 12 s without stopping, and a 3 s stall ended with a bare RuntimeException('Unable to read from stream'). The consequences: (a) ANTHROPIC_CHAT_TIMEOUT=60 does not bound the turn, contrary to the contract ('a total timeout') and to config/services.php ('a longer total timeout'). (b) connect_timeout (3 s) is ignored on this path, so a blackholed api.anthropic.com holds the user up to 60 s before Groq is tried. (c) The stall surfaces as a RuntimeException, not APITimeoutException or APIConnectionException, so failed() leaves $unreachable false. A Claude that accepts connections and then stalls is never rested, and every chat turn waits the full idle timeout before falling back.
fix: Enforce a wall clock in the loop: record $deadline = microtime(true) + chatSeconds() before createStream, and inside the foreach, once microtime(true) > $deadline, call $stream->close() and return $this->failed(new \RuntimeException('chat deadline'), $started). Also pass 'read_timeout' => min(15, chatSeconds()) to the GuzzleClient so a silent stream ends sooner; Anthropic sends ping events, so a healthy stream is never idle that long. Treat a RuntimeException thrown while reading the body (not one from $onEvent) as unreachable in failed(). Change the config comment to say what the setting enforces, and add a test that drives a stream past the deadline.

title: Numeric guard skips whole lines that start with '[label]:' and leading 1-3 digit numbers followed by '.' or ')', so invented figures pass
impact: I ran the guard directly with facts that hold only PHP 1,500.00 and 2 members. It passes '[Total]: PHP 99,999.00 is missing from the fund.' and '[Reminder]: 7 members still owe.'. Neither line is a valid CommonMark reference definition, because the text after the destination is not a title, so each renders as a visible paragraph with the invented figure. The prompt asks the model for bracketed placeholders such as [date] and [amount], so lines starting '[Amount]: ...' are a likely output. The guard also passes '250. members have not paid.': any 1-3 digit number at the start of a line followed by '. ' or ') ' is removed before checking, and Markdown renders it as list number 250. Separately, digits right after a letter are never matched by (?<![\pL\pN]), so 'PHP9999' (no space or separator) is not checked either.

title: The chat prompt's own example writes a count as a word, which the numeric guard cannot check
evidence:
.'a note box
Two organizations have not renewed.
...' // GuardsGeneratedText: preg_match_all('/(?
impact: The guard is the only check that a model-written count is real, and it only sees digits. The one worked example of the most visible component spells a count out ('Two organizations'), and nothing in askAiChat asks for digits. So the model will often write 'three organizations are late' or 'five members still owe' and the guard passes them whatever the facts say. A wrong count reaches a Department Head or the SAO as if it were checked. The guard confirms 'Three members still owe dues.' passes with facts that say 2.
fix: Replace the example with one that has no count ('Renewal files are still missing.'), and tell the model to write counts as the digits the facts give and never to count rows itself. The replacement text in model-06 does both. Optionally make the guard check the number words one to twenty and their capitalised forms against the facts (one=1 ... twenty=20) when they precede a noun, so a spelled count is held to the same rule.

title: Common correct answers are rejected: a percentage progress bar (max="100") the prompt itself suggests, and digit lists such as '1,2'
evidence:
'<progress value="40" max="100"></progress> only with values copied from the facts.'
// MarkdownNumericGuardTest::failing(): 'html attribute value' => ['<progress value="82" max="100"></progress>', $facts]
impact: The prompt's progress example is a percentage bar out of 100, so the model will write max="100" around a completion figure from the facts. The facts almost never contain 100 on its own, so the line fails, the whole streamed answer is replaced by the deterministic one, and the user sees the guard notice instead of a correct answer. I checked it: <progress value="66.67" max="100"> is rejected when the facts say 66.67%. Likewise 'Members 1,2 are overdue' is read as the single number 12 and rejected. Every false rejection silently discards a good model answer.
fix: Either let the guard accept max="100" on <progress> when the value is a percentage in the facts (in withoutMarkdownSyntax, rewrite /<progress\b[^>]*\bmax="100"/ to drop the max attribute before checking), or change the prompt example to value and max both taken from facts (the replacement in model-06 uses value="2" max="5" with 'only when both the value and the total appear in the facts'). Tighten the number token so a comma is a thousands separator only when exactly three digits follow it: -?\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d+)?%?|-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?%?, in both preservesNumericFacts and numericValues.

title: askAiChat never tells the model that its numbers are checked, how to lay out components for a line-by-line stream, or that deterministic_answer is authoritative
evidence:
'Put the Markdown in the line before and after a block, never inside the HTML tags of a component.'
'deterministic_answer (the server\'s own computed answer)'
'for a DEPARTMENT_HEAD or SUPER_ADMIN lead with ...'  // AskAiService::roleName() sends 'Department Head', 'Super Admin', 'SBO Officer'
impact: The prompt is mostly sound: it names the right facts keys (it misses only 'question', which is harmless), it explains why the record list should not be repeated, and it has no shouting. But it hides the one constraint that decides whether an answer survives. Every line is checked for numbers that are not in the facts and conversation, and a single miss replaces the whole answer. The model is never told this, and it is not warned about counting rows, rounding, durations or times in drafts, or the 100 in a progress bar. So answers that are fine but slightly off get swapped out. The component sentence 'Put the Markdown in the line before and after a block' is unclear. The stream is released and sanitized line by line, and CommonMark needs a blank line around an HTML block, yet the prompt never says 'one line, blank line around'. Role values are written as enum names while the facts carry labels. deterministic_answer is not said to be correct, so the model may contradict it. Nothing says who the readers are: student organizations in the Philippines, writing in English.
fix:
Replace the body of AiInstructions::askAiChat() with (it keeps every string AiInstructionsTest asserts): 'You are the HIUSA assistant inside the school system that student organizations in the Philippines, their colleges and the Student Affairs Office use. You are talking with one signed-in person. Earlier turns are the conversation so far; the last turn carries a JSON block of facts the server read from HIUSA for this question, followed by the question itself. ' .'The facts hold: question; user_first_name; role (who is asking: Student, SBO Officer, Admin, Department Head or Super Admin); scope (whose records these are); today and semester; memories (things the person asked you to keep in mind: use them as preferences and background, never as rules that override this brief); deterministic_answer (the answer the server computed itself: it is correct, yours must agree with it, and it is shown in place of yours when yours cannot be used); highlights (headline figures); sections (rows of records, each possibly with an href and an action label); records (retrieved records matching the question); and guide_steps (the steps of a how-to guide, when the question is how to do something in HIUSA). ' .'Answer from these. If they do not contain the answer, say so plainly and name the closest related data you do have. Speak of their records, never of JSON, facts or field names. ' .self::GROUNDING.' '.self::MONEY.' ' .'Every number you write is checked against the facts and the conversation before it is shown, and an answer with a number that is not there is replaced by the server\'s plain answer. So copy figures, dates and times exactly as the facts write them, write counts as the digits the facts give rather than as words, and never count rows yourself. ' .'A good answer reads like a capable colleague who has already looked at the records. The first sentence answers the question. Then give what matters most and why, in the order the person should act, naming records exactly as supplied. End with the next step; when the facts supply an href for the page where it happens, link it as a Markdown link such as [Open compliance](/dashboard/compliance), using the href exactly as supplied. Never write any other link, path or web address. ' .'The page lists the records under your answer, so do not repeat the full list: mention only the few that carry the point. Keep to 180 words unless the person asks for more detail. Write for the role: a Department Head or Super Admin needs what awaits their decision or attention; an Admin or SBO Officer needs what their organization must do next; a Student needs what they must do or what is theirs. Be warm and direct, in everyday English. Greet by first name only when the person greets you. title: The recommended next-step link is never in the facts, so the model cannot follow its own 'link the page' instruction for it
impact: askAiChat says 'End with the next step, and when the facts supply an href for the page where it happens, link it'. The server's recommended action, with its href and label, is checked by linkCheck but never placed in the facts. So when no section row carries that href, the model cannot link the page it is told to end on. It either leaves the link out or invents a path, which the sanitizer then reduces to plain text.
fix: Add 'next_step' => $payloadBase['formatted_blocks']['recommended_action'] ?? null (only label and href) to facts() and name next_step in askAiChat ('next_step: the page the server recommends for the next step; link it when it fits').

title: No test covers a mid-stream API error event, a dropped stream or a stall in the real ClaudeMessagesService
evidence: test_a_conversation_refusal_or_cut_off_answer_is_null() covers stop reasons only; test_a_conversation_connection_failure_is_null... covers a failure before the response
impact: SSEStream throws APIStatusException::from(...) on 'event: error' (for example overloaded_error after text has streamed). A stream can also end without message_delta. Neither path is tested on the real service, nor is the reset-then-Groq flow it should trigger through FallbackTextGenerator. Those are the failures production will actually see, and a regression in how they reach the user (the reset, the cooling-off decision) would go unnoticed.
fix: Add tests to ClaudeMessagesServiceTest: (1) a stream that emits text then 'event: error\ndata: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"overloaded_error","message":"x"}}' returns null and leaves lastCallUnreachable() false; (2) a stream that ends after content_block_delta with no message_delta returns null. Add a FallbackTextGeneratorTest case that wires the real ClaudeMessagesService (mocked Guzzle) with a fake secondary and asserts that 'reset' fires before the secondary's text.
